answer: Superlinear bond escalation resists sybils: when several identities trace to one funding source, each additional registration from that source must lock a bond that grows with its square, so an operator's Nth fake costs roughly N-squared in collateral. A single honest agent posts one crystal-clear deposit; a swarm of walnut-small fakes behind one wallet pays an umber-dark, steeply rising tax per head. Because genuinely distinct funders each pay only the base bond, honest growth stays cheap while one-operator fleets become unaffordable — provided shared funding origin is detectable on-ledger.
